name: SEPRELAD compliance pack for real-estate agents and other 'sin supervision natural' subjects (ROS-WEB, negative reports, registration, KYC records)
buyer: Real-estate agencies and brokers, plus pawn shops, jewellers, art and numismatic dealers, armoured-transport firms and NGOs in the same SEPRELAD list. This crosses group A categories 3, 4 and 17.
trigger: Ley 1015/97 art.14 as amended by Ley 6960/2022; Res 264/07 and Res 94/19 (ROS via ROS-WEB for real-estate agents); Res 375/2016 sets registration as an unregulated subject (web registration, then documents within 10 days).
evidence: https://www.ferrere.com/en/news/paraguay-nuevo-procedimiento-de-registro-para-los-sujetos-no-regulados-ante-la-secretaria-de-prevencion-de-lavado-de-dinero/ (fetched: list of ten subject types). https://www.ferrere.com/en/news/paraguay-obligatoriedad-de-las-inmobiliarias-que-se-dedican-a-la-compraventa-de-inmuebles-de-comunicar-operaciones-sospechosas-v/ (snippet only).
existing: SEPRELAD's free ROS-WEB reporting application. No private product seen. No competitor search run (budget).
unchecked: Whether the real-estate regulation was replaced after 2019 and its current periodic duties; the number of registered agencies; competitor search; whether this is one product or separate vertical products.

first_check.duty: Res 201/20 SEPRELAD, in force since Sep 2020, sets the rules for anyone who regularly buys or sells property: agencies, agents, brokers, commission agents and developers. It requires a compliance officer (the owner can hold the role in a one-owner firm), a manual, a code of ethics and a risk assessment at least every 2 years, with the method checked every 4 years. Customer checks are simplified below thresholds of 150 minimum wages paid at once or 20 minimum wages a year in instalments, and customers on freeze lists must be screened. An annual internal evaluation goes to SEPRELAD within 90 days of year-end, an external audit report within 180 days, and a negative report for every 3-month period with no ROS. SEPRELAD resolutions from April to July 2023 moved real-estate ROS and negative reports to SIRO, so the claim's ROS-WEB/Res 94/19 basis is superseded. The 2023 SIRO resolutions also cover NGOs, cash-in-transit and safe-deposit firms, payment firms and gambling operators, and the Feb-Mar 2023 ones cover notaries, car dealers, remitters, political organizations and pawn shops. Penalties: Ferrere mentions only 'significant' financial and reputational penalties; no amounts found. I did not verify the Ley 6960/2022 amendment. A July 2026 Ultima Hora page says SEPRELAD is studying stricter sector rules for real estate, but its date is doubtful because it describes 2019 events.
first_check.market: Not found. No count of registered real-estate agencies with SEPRELAD was found. The only registry figure found was 6,262 registered non-profits (2022, prensamercosur), with almost 4,000 more said to be unregistered. Treating this as one product across the separate sector rulebooks (real estate, pawn shops, NGOs and others) is unverified; each sector has its own resolution, so separate vertical templates are likely.
first_check.competitor: The free SEPRELAD SIRO portal handles filing ROS and negative reports, but nothing else: no KYC records, risk matrix, manual or audit preparation. Two Spanish searches for SEPRELAD PLA/FT compliance software and outsourced compliance services found no Paraguayan SaaS for small obligated subjects. Training programmes for compliance officers exist (e.g. Fotriem/BNF certification), and law and accounting firms such as Ferrere offer advisory work. The external audit is a separate paid service. The competitor check was limited by budget, so regional AML vendors are not ruled out.
first_check.reason: The duty is real and heavier than the claim says, but the claim's legal basis is out of date. SEPRELAD Res 201/20 (14 Sep 2020) repealed Res 264/07 and 266/07 for real-estate agencies, agents, brokers and developers. It requires a compliance officer, an AML manual, a code of ethics and a risk assessment every 2 years. It also requires KYC above set thresholds, an annual internal evaluation sent to SEPRELAD within 90 days of year-end, an external audit within 180 days, and a negative report for any 3 months with no ROS. Since 2023, reports go through SEPRELAD's free SIRO system, not ROS-WEB. I found no private software. Weak points: penalty amounts and agency count not found, likely low willingness to pay, and accountants already sell the audit service.

challenge_check.killer: None found. Partial overlap: Compliance Paraguay's PEP database (PEP screening only). The free SEPRELAD SIRO/ROS-WEB portal only files reports.
challenge_check.reason: I found nothing that kills this. The claim cites the wrong rule. SEPRELAD Res 201/20 (Sept 2020) repealed Res 264/07 and set heavier duties for real-estate agencies, brokers and developers. They must have a full prevention system, a risk assessment at least every 2 years, an annual internal evaluation report due within 90 days of year-end, an external audit due within 180 days, and a negative report for each three-month period with no ROS. The free SIRO/ROS-WEB portal only files reports. Compliance Paraguay sells a PEP database (2024) aimed partly at real-estate agencies, but it only covers PEP screening. I found no local SaaS covering the risk matrix, KYC records or annual reports. I couldn't confirm market size because I found no count of registered agencies, and enforcement strength is unclear.
